item.text: {"question_id":"5B.8","answer":"In 2023, Lula’s government adopted or restored several potentially redistributive measures: Bolsa Família provided per-member, early-childhood, pregnancy, and youth benefits and preferentially paid the family’s woman; the program reached more than 21 million families according to a contemporary policy review. Minha Casa, Minha Vida’s low-income track allowed subsidies of up to 95%, and the minimum wage rose 3% in real terms, increasing benefits tied to the wage floor. A racial-equality package and equal-pay law were also enacted. These measures demonstrate policy direction and some implementation, but the supplied evidence does not establish their full incidence across tax classes, regions, genders, and groups. The TCU found that the inherited R$600-per-family component reduced per-capita equity and continued to favor single-person families; it also estimated 2.2 million excess beneficiary families, identified deficient regional-coverage indicators, and warned of possible formalization disincentives. CadÚnico weaknesses further created risks of erroneous payments, although the audit findings do not establish personal presidential responsibility or intentional targeting. Outcomes remained highly unequal: 28.8 million children were in multidimensional poverty in 2023; food insecurity disproportionately affected Black families; 63% of Black female-headed households were below the poverty line; 39 million people worked informally; 2 million children and adolescents were out of school, 63% of them Black; and UNESCO identifies significant education-quality disparities between public and private institutions and across regions, without Lula-specific attribution. The 2023 income-tax schedule records rates and thresholds but supplies no incidence evidence. Earlier minimum-wage and poverty trends cannot be treated as 2023 outcomes attributable to this ruler-period. Overall, the evidence supports a mixed and incomplete distributional record: substantial targeted policy and reach, but documented design, targeting, regional-measurement, labor-formalization, and persistent group-disparity
